words.gloss: than those who have undertaken murder

literal: Than those who have undertaken murder, more cruel indeed is the king who, having undertaken harassment, conducts himself doing unjust things.
translation: More cruel than those who make a living by murder is the king who oppresses his subjects and rules with injustice.
modern: கொலை செய்வதைத் தொழிலாகக் கொண்டவர்களை விட, தன் குடிமக்களைத் துன்புறுத்தி அறமல்லாத செயல்களைச் செய்து வாழும் அரசன் மிகவும் கொடியவன் ஆவான்.
explanation: This couplet compares a tyrannical ruler to murderers. The poet states that a king who oppresses his subjects ('அலை மேற்கொண்டு') and acts unjustly ('அல்லவை செய்து') is far more cruel ('கொடிதே') than those who commit murder ('கொலை மேற்கொண்டார்'). While murderers kill individuals, an unjust ruler destroys the livelihood and peace of an entire nation. The key words 'அலை' (harassment/oppression) and 'அல்லவை' (unjust deeds) highlight the destructive nature of bad governance.
